_doc: Words no ad the studio offers should carry by default. ONE list, read by scripts/ad_census.mjs (DESIGN-LAW 143): every word on every offered ad, as a visitor opens it, is matched against it, and --gate fails an ad that carries one. Started 2026-11-18 from docs/COMPETITOR-RESEARCH-2026-11-12.md section 5.2 ('What to leave out'), with the house's own lists that say the same thing beside it: the full ad's pre-flight (motion/fullad.js fullWords, PROOF: rule 138), rule 55 (no dollar figure, no invented proof, no deadline, no dash in customer copy) and rule 136 (a phone ad asks for a text, not a picture). Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions, matched case-insensitively on the ad's words with accents kept (the census upper-cases them first). 'unless': the entry is not matched when this pattern is also in the same line (a limit given). 'only': the entry applies to ads of these categories alone. 'say': what a customer who typed the phrase is told, in their words (rule 113): the site reads this list through motion/banned-words.js, written from it by scripts/build_banned_words.mjs, since spec/ is not served. To add a phrase, add a row; to retire one, delete it. A customer's own typed words are theirs: the census types only a number, a website, a business name and an area, so every other word it finds is the studio's.

phrases.label: UP TO $
phrases.why: Read as the typical price and flagged by regulators; the pre-flight says it too.
phrases.say: "Up to" a price is read as the usual price. Name what you pay for one model, or leave the price out.

phrases.label: TOP DOLLAR
phrases.why: The most generic phrase in the category: on sign-shop posters and the franchise's captions, so it says nothing about who is buying.
phrases.say: TOP DOLLAR is on every buyer's sign, so it tells people nothing about you. Your business name or your town says more.

phrases.label: HIGHEST
phrases.why: A comparative claim that may need proof.
phrases.say: "Highest" is a claim you may be asked to prove. "Fair offer" says it without the risk.

phrases.label: BEST PRICE
phrases.why: A comparative claim that may need proof.
phrases.say: "Best price" is a claim you may be asked to prove. "Fair offer" says it without the risk.

phrases.label: WE BEAT ANY OFFER
phrases.why: A comparative claim that may need proof.
phrases.say: "We beat any offer" is a promise you may be asked to keep. "Fair offer" says it without the risk.

phrases.label: ANY CONDITION (no limit)
phrases.why: With no limit it reads as no questions asked.
phrases.say: "Any condition" with no limit reads as no questions asked. Say what you take, like CRACKED OK, or what you do not, like NOT LOCKED.

phrases.label: ICLOUD LOCKED / OK
phrases.why: Reads as no questions asked; the category has a documented stolen-goods problem.
phrases.say: Saying locked or blacklisted phones are fine reads as no questions asked. Leave it out.

phrases.label: NO TITLE, NO PROBLEM
phrases.say: "No title" reads as no questions asked. Ask for the title instead.

phrases.label: TODAY ONLY / HURRY / DON'T WAIT
phrases.why: The FTC's named pressure signal; rule 55 allows urgency only when it is true.
phrases.say: "Today only", "hurry" and "don't wait" read as pressure. Say it only when the offer really ends.

phrases.label: #1 / NUMBER ONE
phrases.say: "#1" is a claim you may be asked to prove. Leave it out.

phrases.label: BEST
phrases.why: A claim that needs proof (BEST PRICE is its own row).
phrases.say: "Best" is a claim you may be asked to prove. "Fair" or "honest" says it without the risk.

phrases.label: FASTEST / LOWEST / UNBEATABLE / MOST MONEY
phrases.say: "Fastest", "lowest" or "unbeatable" is a claim you may be asked to prove. Leave it out.

phrases.label: GUARANTEED
phrases.say: "Guaranteed" is a promise you may be asked to keep. Leave it out.

phrases.label: a dollar figure
phrases.why: Prices move and a picture does not: no dollar figure on a graphic by default (an owner-entered, dated price line is the research's own proposal, 5.1 no. 3). An UP TO price is its own row.
phrases.say: A price on a picture goes out of date while the picture keeps being shared. Leave the dollar figure out.

phrases.label: SINCE 20XX / stars / review counts
phrases.say: Stars, review counts and "since" years have to be true and shown somewhere. Leave them out unless they are.

phrases.label: an en or em dash
phrases.why: No em or en dash in anything a customer reads.
phrases.say: The long dash is not used on our ads. Use a comma or the word "to".

phrases.label: TEXT A PIC (phone ads)
phrases.why: A phone ad asks for a text (the IMEI), not a picture: the buyer's chatbot quotes from what is typed.
phrases.say: On a phone ad, ask for a text, not a picture: TEXT US NOW or TEXT YOUR IMEI gets a quote faster.
